comments.content: `FINAL_LIBS` already includes `$(RDMA_LIBS)` on the previous line, and this line appends `$(RDMA_LIBS)` again. This duplicates the RDMA libraries in the link line for the server. Remove the redundant `$(RDMA_LIBS)` here.

When `rdma` is non-zero but `USE_RDMA` is not defined, the function silently falls through without initializing `options` (no TCP options are set). This will produce a broken connection attempt. Either guard the caller so `rdma` can only be set when `USE_RDMA` is defined, or return an error/fallback to TCP here.

Calling `writeHandler` directly here (and similarly in `createClient`) bypasses the event loop and can recurse or run before the client is fully initialized. In particular, `writeHandler` may call `resetClient`/`freeClient` and manipulate the event loop while we are still inside `resetClient`/`createClient`. Consider scheduling the write via the event loop or deferring it until after initialization completes.

Same concern as in `resetClient`: invoking `writeHandler` directly from `createClient` can run before the client is fully set up and may re-enter client lifecycle code. Prefer registering the event or deferring the initial write.

`getValkeyContext` is called with `rdma=0` here even when the user requested `--rdma`. If cluster configuration fetching should also use RDMA, pass `config.rdma`; otherwise this is intentional but worth confirming, since the rest of the benchmark uses RDMA.
Same as above: cluster slot configuration connections ignore `config.rdma`. Confirm whether RDMA should be used for these auxiliary connections.
The FCALL setup connection also passes `rdma=0`, ignoring `config.rdma`. If RDMA is requested, this connection will use TCP, which may be inconsistent with the rest of the benchmark run.

After reconnecting with RDMA, the code still checks `config.tls` and calls `cliSecureConnection`. RDMA and TLS are likely mutually exclusive; if both flags are set this may fail or be meaningless. Consider rejecting the combination at option parsing time.

`clusterManagerNodeConnect` now uses `config.rdma` for cluster manager connections. Ensure this is intended, since cluster manager operations may not support RDMA and could break cluster commands when `--rdma` is passed.

`clusterManagerCommandImport` connects to the source node using `config.rdma`. If the source node does not support RDMA, this will fail. Consider using TCP for the import source or documenting the requirement.

The `ENABLE_RDMA` cache variable is set but never used to actually enable RDMA in the libvalkey subdirectory (unlike `ENABLE_TLS`). Verify that libvalkey's CMake reads `ENABLE_RDMA`; otherwise this block has no effect.
